subject: ventures/stripe-payout-to-journal
professional: a bookkeeper or accountant who closes month-end for Stripe merchants and posts payout journals into Xero or QuickBooks; they check first that gross sales, Stripe fees, refunds and disputes are booked separately with the right signs, that a payout straddling a month end lands in two periods, that the payout ties to the bank deposit, that failed payouts and reversals do not double-count, and that the file actually imports into their ledger

evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (352 lines, pure functions, integer cents), the index.html module script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Good: output escaped before innerHTML, quoted-CSV splitter handles doubled quotes, IIF strips tabs and newlines from account names (tested), UTF-16 BOM decoding. Defects: ventures/sales-export-to-journal/engines/stripe.mjs is a byte-identical copy of calc.mjs (diff -q: identical) with no test or script keeping them in sync, and the same journal/export code is repeated in at least 10 other *-to-journal ventures; the page parses the deposit with its own parseFloat (index.html:164) instead of the library's tested parseAmount; categoryOf's FEE_CATS regex (calc.mjs:169) uses '.*_fee' so any future '*_fee' type, including platform income (application_fee), silently becomes a fee expense instead of reaching the uncategorised safety net.
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer and no-warranty footer (page.test.mjs:7), not-affiliated clause (page.test.mjs:38), 'a test in the code asserts there are no network calls' (page.test.mjs:17, a static regex), layouts 'read from memory of public help documents' disclosed in header and footer (page.test.mjs:31), 'never dropped' for unknown categories (calc.test.mjs:51), usage events named on the page are the ones recorded (page.test.mjs:49), 'clearing account returns to zero' holds whenever every payout is deposited. Not backed: README.md:21 test command fails on Node 22; 'European 1.234,56 and US 1,234.56 both work' (index.html:106) is true of report rows but not of the deposit box on the same page; the account box and download note (index.html:77, index.html:100) say accounts may be 'names or codes', but the Xero column written is *AccountCode and every default name is 11 to 20 characters (Xero account codes are at most 10), so the default Xero file would not import as written (from Xero's manual-journal import help, not verified live). llms.txt lists a github.io URL; the Pages build rewrites that host (platform/ci/build_pages_site.py:51 DEFAULT_BASE_URL), so it is source-only.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a bookkeeper downloads the itemised payout reconciliation report, pastes it, types the bank deposit, maps accounts, downloads a Xero journal. For a single sub-1,000 payout with charges, refunds, disputes and fees this produces a correct, month-split, balanced journal. A practitioner hits in the first hour: the deposit typed as '1,234.56' is rejected as a mismatch; the default Xero file carries account names in the *AccountCode column; real Stripe payout IDs are 27 characters, so the QBO JournalNo becomes 'po_...-2026-09' at 35 characters, longer than QuickBooks Online's 21-character journal number (from QBO API DocNumber limit, not verified live); nothing has been checked against a real Stripe export or a live import (VENTURE.yaml). One payout or file at a time, no saved mapping.
evidence.domain: Compared with the standard clearing-account method used by A2X and recommended by Stripe-specialist bookkeepers: gross sales credited, processing fees debited to an expense, refunds and disputes as contra-revenue, the dispute fee as a fee not a dispute (tested), each period's net to a Stripe clearing account that the bank deposit clears, period cut-off by the balance transaction's created date, rows never dropped. That is what a senior bookkeeper would sign off for ordinary charge/refund/dispute payouts, with tax split and revenue recognition stated as out of scope. Departures: payout_reversal (a failed payout's funds returning) is booked to Adjustments instead of against clearing, double-counting the funds; type-only files put application_fee (platform income) into the Stripe fees expense; reserve categories risk_reserved_funds/connect_reserved_funds are not recognised (flagged, not dropped) while the rule lists invented names reserve_hold/reserve_release; created dates are used as written (UTC by default) with no time-zone choice for the month cut-off.

defects.what: The deposit box parses '1,234.56' (and '1.234,56') as 1.23: parseFloat after replacing only the first comma. Every payout of 1,000 or more typed with a thousands separator gets a false 'rows add up to X but the payout is 1.23' error. Fix: use the library's parseAmount, which already handles both forms.

payout_reversal (a failed payout's funds returning to the balance) is booked to Stripe Adjustments instead of against Stripe clearing, so the failed payout's amount is counted twice (once in the original payout's journal, again as an adjustment credit) and clearing keeps the undeposited balance; the reconciliation still says both payouts agree. Unverified against a real failed-payout export.

The Xero export writes the mapped account into *AccountCode, but the default mapping is names of 11 to 20 characters ('Stripe Uncategorised'); Xero account codes are at most 10 characters and must match an existing code, so the default Xero file would not import. The page says 'names or codes' (index.html:77, :100) without saying Xero needs codes.

Five of seven seeded mutations survive: refund_failure and payout_reversal categories, the mixed-currency warning, the month-end dating of a payout whose rows are all in an earlier month, and the expected-deposit guard for multi-payout files are untested.
README test command 'node --test ventures/stripe-payout-to-journal/' fails on Node 22; the working form is cd into the folder and run node --test '*.test.mjs'.

QBO JournalNo and IIF DOCNUM are the payout ID plus '-YYYY-MM'; with a real 27-character po_ ID that is 35 characters, over QuickBooks Online's 21-character journal number limit (Intuit API DocNumber, not verified live).

FEE_CATS matches any '.*_fee', so in a type-only balance export application_fee (a platform's income) is booked as a reduction of the Stripe fees expense instead of reaching the uncategorised safety net; the rule also lists reserve_hold/reserve_release, which are not Stripe reporting categories, while risk_reserved_funds and connect_reserved_funds are missed.
ventures/sales-export-to-journal/engines/stripe.mjs is a byte-identical copy of calc.mjs with no sync check, so a fix here does not reach the hub tool.
Column layouts and category values have never been checked against a real Stripe export or a live Xero/QuickBooks import (stated in VENTURE.yaml and on the page).

verdict: The journal engine is sound accounting for an ordinary Stripe payout: on four hand recomputations (the sample's two month-split journals, a fee-returning refund with a dispute lost and won, a Title Case balance export with thousands separators, a JPY payout) every line and the clearing total matched, and the method (gross sales, fees, contra refunds and disputes, a clearing account cleared by the deposit, period by created date) is what a senior bookkeeper uses. It misses the bar on correctness, verification and claims: the page's deposit box reads '1,234.56' as 1.23, a failed payout's returning funds are booked as an adjustment and double-counted, the default Xero export puts long account names in the code column, five of seven seeded mutations survive, the README test command fails, and nothing has been tried against a real Stripe export or a live import. Finished (every listed feature works in node), not at the senior-professional bar.
